message.content:
Nxeon (VPS/game-hosting business, production Next.js app at /opt/nxeon). Two real regressions the owner just reported from live screenshots, after tonight's NxLabs marketing overhaul (a large batch of commits, newest around `0436a8b0de`/`9ea365d71b`/`6ac103eae5` — read `git log --oneline -20` for full context).

## Bug 1 — carousel cards are not clickable, on BOTH the marketing and portal pages

The owner: "none of the options in the carousels on the portal or the marketing page are clickable." This affects BOTH carousel types built tonight:
- `components/mods/GameCatalogueCarousel.tsx` (the "Browse by game" game-catalogue row)
- `components/mods/ModCarouselRow.tsx` (the Featured/Most Downloaded/Recently Updated/Top Rated mod rows — this one was restructured a few hours ago by a different fix to take pre-rendered `<ModCard>` children instead of importing ModCard directly, to fix an unrelated build-breaking bug; that restructure is NOT necessarily the cause of this click bug, but read it carefully anyway since it's recent).

**Read both files in full.** My strong suspicion, which you must verify (not just assume): both use a manual pointer-drag-to-scroll mechanism — `onPointerDown` calls `track.setPointerCapture(e.pointerId)` unconditionally for non-touch pointers, `onPointerMove` sets `moved = true` once `Math.abs(dx) > 3`, and `onPointerUp` installs a one-time capturing `click` listener that calls `preventDefault()`/`stopPropagation()` ONLY when `moved` was true. On paper this should only suppress a click after real drag distance — but real mice/trackpads often report a few pixels of jitter even on a stationary click, and `setPointerCapture` on the track element can itself interfere with how the browser subsequently routes the click to the nested `<Link>` inside `<ModCard>`/the game tile, depending on browser. Test this for real in an actual browser (Playwright, but ALSO consider that Playwright's synthetic clicks might not reproduce the exact same jitter a real mouse does — if Playwright clicks work fine but the owner's real clicks don't, that itself is a clue pointing at the jitter/capture theory, not a totally broken href).

Also check for something dumber and equally plausible: is the `<Link>` (or its container) getting a `pointer-events: none` from somewhere, or is the invisible `absolute inset-0` arrow-button overlay row (`z-20`) sized/positioned in a way that sits ON TOP of the cards and intercepts clicks even outside the actual button hitboxes (check the `pointer-events-none`/`pointer-events-auto` split on that overlay row carefully — a mistake there would make an entire row of cards unclickable except where a real click happens to land exactly on a 40px arrow button)?

Fix the real root cause once found — don't just paper over it. A common correct fix for exactly this class of bug: only treat a pointer sequence as a "drag" (and only then suppress the resulting click) past a higher, more deliberate threshold (e.g. 8-10px, not 3px), AND/or don't call `setPointerCapture` until movement has already been confirmed past that threshold (so a plain click never invokes capture at all), AND/or scope the drag-to-scroll listeners to only actually engage for mouse (not needed at all for touch/trackpad, which already get native scroll — re-check whether `e.pointerType === "touch"` is the only exclusion, or whether trackpad-originated pointer events report as "mouse" and are wrongly caught by this logic too).

## Bug 2 — mod detail page hero art is "still not the way I want," per a real screenshot

A live screenshot of the PORTAL mod detail page (`/dashboard/nxlabs/rust/stack-size-controller` or similar — "Stack Size Controller", Rust) shows the hero area behind "NxLabs / Stack Size Controller" still nearly solid dark/navy with no visible Rust key art — despite an earlier fix tonight ("root-caused and fixed on both detail pages and both family pages... confirmed via screenshot: CS2's hero art is now clearly visible"). Investigate why this specific case (Rust, portal mod detail page) still looks broken when CS2 was reportedly verified fixed:
- Check if the portal mod detail page (`app/dashboard/nxlabs/[family]/[slug]/page.tsx`) actually got the same fix as the marketing one (`app/(marketing)/mods/[family]/[slug]/page.tsx`) — re-verify, don't trust the prior report blindly.
- Check if this is a PER-GAME issue — maybe Rust's specific hero image file (`public/games/art/rust_hero.jpg` or whatever `GAME_ART_SLUG.rust.hero` resolves to) is itself darker/lower-contrast than CS2's, making the SAME gradient math look "broken" for this game even though the code is technically correct — if so, this needs a per-image or more conservative universal gradient adjustment, not just confirming the code path exists.
- Get the ACTUAL original ask right by re-reading it carefully: the owner's request was "I want the hero section for the mod page to have game hero image in the background" — take a real screenshot of the current live state (both marketing and portal, for at least 2-3 different games including Rust) and compare directly against this ask and against `.design-refs/nxlabs/mod-page-marketing.png` / `mod-page-portal.png` (the literal approved mockups) — if the current implementation still doesn't match what those mockups show, fix it to actually match, don't just confirm the code "does something."

## CRITICAL process rule (still in force)
Multiple agents running their own `deploy-staging.sh`/`promote-production.sh` concurrently corrupted the build output earlier tonight and caused a real production outage. **Do NOT run `deploy-staging.sh` or `promote-production.sh` yourself.** Before starting, run `ps aux | grep -E "next build|deploy-staging|promote-production"` — if anything is running, wait. Make your changes, verify with `npx tsc --noEmit`, commit and push to `main`, then STOP. I (the parent session) will deploy it myself once you're done — this is a live, actively-reported production bug affecting real clickability, so I'll deploy promptly once you report back, don't sit on a finished fix.

## Process (mandatory)
- Read `GameCatalogueCarousel.tsx`, `ModCarouselRow.tsx`, both mod detail page files, and the mockup PNGs in full before making changes.
- Real Playwright verification: actually click a carousel card (not just check the DOM/href exists) and confirm real navigation happens, on both carousel types, on both marketing and portal.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
- Commit and push to `main`.

Report back: the exact root cause of the click bug (with real evidence, not a guess), confirmation clicking now actually navigates on both carousel types, and confirmation the hero art now genuinely matches the approved mockup for multiple games including Rust specifically.

content.thinking: Good, nothing's running now, so I'll go ahead and read the relevant files.

Both files share nearly identical structure. I'm examining the overlay div, which stretches across the full width and height of its container using absolute positioning, but only becomes visible as a flex layout on small screens and up, while remaining pointer-events-none by default.

Since only the two buttons inside get pointer-events-auto, clicks should pass through everywhere else in the row—so the overlay isn't actually blocking anything despite sitting on top with a higher z-index. That rules out the overlay as the bug, which pushes me back toward examining the drag logic, specifically the unconditional pointer capture call on pointer down.

Real mice generate tiny pointermove jitters even during a stationary click, and with only a 3px threshold, that jitter could easily flip `moved` to true for a genuine click. If that happens, the pointerup handler would attach a one-time capturing click listener that calls preventDefault and stopPropagation—swallowing the browser's subsequent click event and blocking the Link's navigation entirely.

This matches the hypothesis: since Playwright's synthetic clicks don't generate that intermediate jitter, they navigate fine, but real users' clicks fail because the 3px threshold is too sensitive to hand tremor. I should also check whether trackpad-originated pointer events might report pointerType "mouse" rather than "touch" on certain browsers/OS combos, which could affect how the exclusion logic applies.

The fix is to raise the movement threshold to something like 8-10px, and more importantly, defer calling setPointerCapture until the movement threshold is actually exceeded rather than on pointerdown itself, so a plain click never triggers capture logic at all. I'm restructuring the pointer handlers to introduce a DRAG_THRESHOLD constant and only invoke capture once real drag movement is detected.

Finishing pointer release logic, then reconsidering: since scrollLeft only updates once the drag threshold is exceeded, small movements before that point won't cause any scrolling, which is the intended click-vs-drag distinction.

Increasing the threshold to around 8-10px should also help with trackpad taps being misread as drags, since real horizontal panning already fires native scroll events separately. I don't think pointerType needs special-casing for pen input.

Next I want to actually verify this fix works with a real Playwright test rather than just reasoning about it, so I'll check the overlay behavior and the hero section next.
I'm comparing the hero JSX section between the marketing page and the portal to see how they differ.

content.thinking:
For the marketing section, I'm making it a much taller full-bleed section with a hero image at 60% opacity for game-art style, fading upward from fully opaque at the bottom to lighter near the top using a top-directed gradient overlay.

For the portal version though, the hero is a much more compact card (min-height 200px, rounded corners, subtle border), using a hardcoded navy color instead of the theme variable for its gradient, with icon and author content overlaid directly in that small box — meaning the content likely sits close to the bottom where the gradient is most opaque, ensuring readability against the background image.

So a fix was already applied here, softening the gradient stops from the old heavier value to the current lighter ones, but it's clearly still not enough for Rust's screenshot showing a nearly solid dark panel with no visible art. Given the min-h-[200px] container only actually fills to about 112px with the icon and padding, the compact size itself may be part of why the darkening reads as overwhelming compared to the marketing hero's much larger canvas.

Also the image itself likely has its own opacity applied via CSS before the gradient overlay stacks on top, so the two darkening effects compound. Given how short the box is, the dark portion dominates the visible thumbnail while only a small top sliver stays lighter, which explains why the compact portal box looks almost solid dark.

The root cause of Bug 2 is that the portal detail page's hero uses a fixed 200px-tall panel, far shorter than marketing's full-bleed hero with generous padding. The same gradient that looks fine on marketing's tall hero collapses into mostly-dark territory in this compact box, since the lighter portion only occupies a thin band at the top while the icon row content sits where the gradient is nearly opaque.

To fix this, I'd need to increase the portal hero's minimum height (maybe to 280px or more) to better match marketing's proportions, and/or lighten the gradient overlay specifically for the portal variant since it's percentage-based across the container height — the shorter box means proportionally more of the "dark" gradient territory covers the visible content.

Alternatively, maybe it's actually the source art itself that's darker for Rust versus other games. I should check the actual hero images on disk and compare brightness, and look at the GAME_ART_SLUG mapping to find where those images live.

input.title: Fix same click-drag jitter bug in GameCoverCarousel
input.tldr: While root-causing tonight's "carousel cards not clickable" bug in GameCatalogueCarousel.tsx and ModCarouselRow.tsx, I found the homepage hero carousel (components/marketing/showcase/GameCoverCarousel.tsx) has the identical latent defect: a small ~4px drag threshold plus unconditional setPointerCapture on pointerdown, which can swallow a real click's navigation after ordinary mouse jitter. It wasn't part of tonight's reported regression and wasn't touched tonight, so I left it alone, but it should get the same fix (raise the threshold, defer capture until real movement) since it can misfire the same way for any real click.
input.prompt: In /opt/nxeon (production Next.js app), components/marketing/showcase/GameCoverCarousel.tsx implements pointer-drag-to-scroll for the homepage's hero game-cover carousel (around lines 355-420: onDown/onMove/onUp inside the "pointer / touch momentum drag" useEffect). It has the same latent bug just fixed tonight in components/mods/GameCatalogueCarousel.tsx and components/mods/ModCarouselRow.tsx (see their onPointerDown/onPointerMove/onPointerUp and the "FIXED 2026-09-20" comments there for the full root-cause writeup): the drag-movement threshold is only 4px (`if (Math.abs(dx) > 4) moved = true;`), and `vp.setPointerCapture?.(e.pointerId)` is called unconditionally in onDown before any movement is observed. Ordinary mouse/trackpad jitter on a stationary click can exceed 4px, which sets `moved = true` and causes onUp to install a capturing one-time `click` listener that calls stopPropagation()/preventDefault(), potentially swallowing real clicks on interactive elements inside the carousel (the player-slot buttons already have their own explicit workaround via `.closest("button")` in onDown, but any real link/card click elsewhere in the carousel is still exposed to this). Apply the same fix pattern used in the two files above: raise the movement threshold to something past normal click jitter (8-10px), and defer `setPointerCapture` until real movement past that threshold is confirmed, so a plain click never triggers capture or the click-swallowing listener. Verify with `npx tsc --noEmit` in /opt/nxeon, then real Playwright verification (a mouse.move/down/move(small jitter)/up sequence, not a synthetic .click()) that a normal click still works on interactive content in this carousel and that real drag-to-scroll still works too. Do not run deploy-staging.sh or promote-production.sh — commit and push to main and stop there.

Comparing the portal's hero image overlay structure to the marketing section's version, I notice the portal uses a contained relative div with an absolute image and gradient overlay, while marketing wraps its image absolutely inside a -z-10 layer behind the content rail. That difference in stacking approach is likely the source of the visual mismatch I need to fix.

I'll make two coordinated changes: substantially increase the portal hero container height (roughly doubling it from 200px) so the fallback art actually reads, and make the gradient/opacity treatment more forgiving for the "heroIsGameArt" fallback case across both marketing and portal, since the Rust data shows the current numbers are marginal even in the taller marketing box.

This confirms marketing's current formula works fine with its generously tall box, so I shouldn't touch marketing's numbers and risk regressing something already working; the scoped fix is specifically the portal box height.

Since portal can't bleed full page-width (fixed content column per existing code), I'm settling on increasing the box height from 200px to 320px, softening the gradient stops slightly to be more forgiving, and bumping the opacity a bit higher for the heroIsGameArt case.

I want to apply this change only to the portal page, since marketing already looks correct in both games per screenshot verification. Now I need to check how the icon and author row is positioned within the container once I increase the height — it sits in normal flow after the absolutely-positioned image and gradient layers, so I need to trace through whether it stays anchored at the top or needs explicit positioning to land at the bottom.

Since the child's natural height (~128px) is less than min-h-[200px], the min-height wins and there's about 72px of empty space below the icon row, still showing background. That means the gradient's opacity is inverted from what I'd want: the top (where the icon sits) is least darkened while the bottom (empty space) is most opaque — which seems backwards for making the icon readable.

So that's actually the lightest zone where the image shows best, meaning my original theory that content sits where the gradient is opaque was backwards. Rereading the code comment, it seems to reference the old `via-navy-950/75` stop being heaviest right where the icon row sits, which implies the layout or gradient stops may have shifted between versions—I need to check how the icon row's ~128px actually maps onto the box's percentage-based gradient stops given the current min-height.

Continuing the interpolation, at the bottom of the icon row the overlay comes out to about 60% opaque navy, versus only 10% at the very top — so the gradient does darken noticeably across the icon row's own height. Since the icon is 64px tall and centered with padding, this means the icon itself sits within that darkening range.

So the icon overlay only produces roughly 18-41% darkening, but I also need to factor in the image's own 60% opacity against the dark background beneath it—meaning actual brightness is the pixel value times 0.6 times the remaining light after the overlay. At the top of the icon that works out to a fairly dim factor around 0.49.

Applying this to rust_hero.jpg, whose top region is naturally darker (~32% brightness), the resulting on-screen brightness lands around 16%—essentially reading as solid dark navy, matching exactly what the owner reported. By contrast, CS2's brighter top region (~69%) ends up around 33% brightness at the same factor, staying clearly visible. This confirms both the opacity stacking and the image's own inherent darkness are compounding to cause the issue.

Rather than doing fragile per-image brightness analysis tonight, I think the right fix is a more conservative universal adjustment to the "heroIsGameArt" fallback: raising the base image opacity from 60% up to something like 85-90% so it reads as a real backdrop, and lightening the gradient stops so the overlay contributes less darkening in the upper region where content sits.

I also want to increase the box height for more breathing room, but crucially I need to leave marketing's existing values untouched since they're already confirmed to look fine on both CS2 and Rust and are stored as a separate, independently duplicated set of constants from portal's — meaning I can safely change portal alone. I'm double-checking this by working through marketing's actual gradient/opacity math for Rust to confirm why its version holds up while portal's breaks.

So while the overlay percentages follow the same formula in both cases, marketing's taller box means that clean top region translates to far more visible pixels before darkening begins, whereas portal's compact box crams that same lightly-obscured zone into a tiny sliver before the heavier overlay kicks in.

With object-cover, whether the container is wider or narrower than the image's own aspect ratio determines if it crops top/bottom or left/right — a wider container matches to width and crops vertically centered, while a narrower one matches height and crops the sides. The rust image at 1200x675 has an aspect ratio of 1.778, so I need to compare that against each container's actual proportions to know exactly what gets cropped.

Working through the crop math, the visible band spans roughly 20% to 80% of the image height vertically centered, meaning the portal crop excludes the top and bottom 20% of the original image — which I need to compare against my earlier brightness bands (top30/mid40/bot30) to see how they align.

Right, the gradient overlay is fixed to box position regardless of image content, so only the base brightness value changes. Redoing the calc with 110 instead of 82 for portal's visible mid-band still gives an effective brightness around 18%, only marginally better than before, and I need to check CS2's mid-band value which appears slightly lower than expected too.

Honestly, my pixel math has too many unreliable assumptions—portal column width, gamma composite behavior, actual background color—to definitively explain the discrepancy. I should stop estimating manually and just wait for the real before-screenshots of CS2 vs Rust portals to compare visually, which will be far more authoritative. Let me check the monitor for those.

Since `min-height` always constrains the final computed height regardless of the content-derived auto height, the used height becomes max(300px, ~112px) = 300px, and modern browsers correctly re-stretch flex items to fill that min-height-enforced size. This confirms my approach of combining flex, stretch, and min-height on the outer container with flex-1 and items-end inside should render correctly.

content.text:
## Summary

Both regressions are fixed, verified against a real running instance (not just code review), and pushed to `main` (auto-pushed by the repo's `post-commit` hook — confirmed `origin/main` now matches local HEAD at `5e62d8538d`). No build/deploy scripts were run by me, and none were running when I started or when I finished.

### Bug 1 — carousel cards unclickable

**Root cause (confirmed with real evidence, not assumed):** `GameCatalogueCarousel.tsx` and `ModCarouselRow.tsx` both used a 3px "moved" threshold and called `track.setPointerCapture()` unconditionally on `pointerdown`. I reproduced this against the **unmodified production build** (port 3000) with a real Playwright `mouse.move→down→move(~2-4px)→up` sequence — the kind of jitter an ordinary hand produces on a stationary click — and got "DID NOT NAVIGATE" on both carousel types. A zero-movement synthetic `.click()` did *not* reproduce it, which is exactly the tell the task predicted. Once `moved` flips true from jitter alone, `onPointerUp` installs a capturing one-time `click` listener that calls `preventDefault()`/`stopPropagation()` before the click reaches the nested `<Link>`.

I also explicitly ruled out the arrow-overlay theory: the `pointer-events-none`/`pointer-events-auto` split on that row is correct, and `document.elementFromPoint()` at the click coordinates confirmed real clicks land on the card's image/link, never the overlay.

**Fix:** raised the threshold to 8px and deferred `setPointerCapture` until real movement crosses it, so a plain click never triggers capture or the click-swallowing listener at all. Applied identically to both files.

**Verification:** after building the fix in an isolated worktree/dev server (never touching `/opt/nxeon`'s or `nxeon-staging`'s build output), I got 6/6 clean passes across repeated jitter-click attempts on marketing for both carousel types, and confirmed passes on portal for both types too, plus confirmed real drag-to-scroll still works (`scrollLeft` moved 0→208 on an intentional >8px drag). Note: this box is under severe memory pressure tonight from concurrent unrelated builds (60/62GB RAM, swap full at points), which caused some initial false-negative results from dev-server compile latency — resolved by re-testing with pre-warmed routes and repeated attempts until consistent.

Found but **did not touch** (out of scope, flagged separately): `components/marketing/showcase/GameCoverCarousel.tsx` has the identical latent pattern (4px threshold, eager capture) but wasn't part of tonight's regression — spawned as a separate task (`task_6f2dbb47`).

### Bug 2 — Rust hero art still faint on portal mod detail page

**Root cause:** the portal's hero box (`app/dashboard/nxlabs/[family]/[slug]/page.tsx`) is a fixed `min-h-[200px]` — far shorter than the marketing page's full-bleed hero — and `rust_hero.jpg` measures ~63% of `cs2_hero.jpg`'s mean luminance (verified via pixel analysis). The identical gradient math that read fine for CS2 in that short box compounded into a near-featureless dark panel for Rust. Confirmed with real screenshots: portal CS2 looked fine, portal Rust (both `stack-size-controller` and `clans`) looked washed-out/murky — while the *marketing* page's hero for the same Rust image already looked correct (bigger box, more room), so marketing was left untouched.

**Fix:** taller panel (200px→300px, restructured to flexbox so content anchors to the bottom), base image opacity 60%→90%, and a visibly lighter scrim, for the family-fallback art path specifically. Safe to brighten because this box only holds a small icon and (when present) muted author text — no large text needing a dark backdrop.

**Verification:** real after-fix screenshots show Rust now clearly visible/vivid on both mod pages, closely matching CS2's quality and the approved mockup's intent ("game hero image in the background"). Valheim and Palworld (mods with their own icon/screenshot, the *other* code branch) were also screenshotted to confirm that path is unaffected.

### Also found, flagged separately (not fixed, out of scope)
The portal's "What's New" announcement popup never stays dismissed — a fresh account dismisses it, navigates away, and sees it again on the very next page load, repeatedly. Reproduced consistently across many test accounts. Spawned as `task_9ca5446d` for separate investigation (looks like the `markAnnouncementSeen` upsert isn't actually persisting, not a duplicate-rows issue — confirmed only 2 real `PUBLISHED` announcements exist).
